title: Natural coordinates for finite free internal scalar extension
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be an essentially small site with the sheafification and closed symmetric monoidal tensor of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] for abelian sheaves. Let $\varphi:R\to B$ be a morphism of commutative ring objects, and use internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and scalar extension and restriction [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. Suppose given an $R$-module isomorphism $\theta:R^{\oplus n}\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Res}_\varphi B$, for an integer $n\geq0$, with inverse coordinates $q_i:B\to R$. Write $b_i$ for the image of $1$ under the $i$th basis map $R\to B$ (and its restriction on each test object). There is a natural isomorphism of $R$-module valued functors
$$\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\bigl(B\otimes_R-\bigr)\xrightarrow{\sim}(-)^n.$$
For an $R$-module sheaf $M$, it and its inverse are specified on local elementary tensors and tuples by
$$\Phi_M(s\otimes m)=(q_i(s)m)_i,\qquad \Psi_M((m_i)_i)=\sum_i b_i\otimes m_i.$$
These formulas specify sheaf morphisms through the tensor and coequalizer universal properties; no equality of tensor-sheaf sections with sectionwise tensor products is asserted.

proof.text: Work in $H=\operatorname{Sh}(C,\operatorname{Ab})$ with its canonical closed tensor. The sheaf-tensor statement supplies fixed-factor preservation of colimits. Put $N=\operatorname{Res}_\varphi B$ and $E=\operatorname{Res}_\varphi\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi$. Use $U$, $p_M$ and $t_{N,M}$ for the forgetful functor and the two quotient maps of the restricted-extension comparison. Its hypotheses hold for the given commutative $R,B$ and arbitrary $\varphi$. It supplies a natural $R$-linear isomorphism $\kappa_M:E(M)\simeq N\otimes_R M$ with $U\kappa_M\,p_M=t_{N,M}$ and $U\kappa_M^{-1}\,t_{N,M}=p_M$.

source.place: Last sentence, first inference: the natural finite-power description of tensor with a finite free coefficient ring

proof.text: Apply the finite-free relative-tensor coordinate lemma to $N$ and the given $\theta$. Its maps $e_i=\theta\iota_i$ and $q_i=\pi_i\theta^{-1}$ are exactly this basis and its inverse coordinates. It supplies $D_{\theta,M}:N\otimes_R M\simeq M^n$ naturally in $M$. Set $\Phi_M=D_{\theta,M}\circ\kappa_M$ and $\Psi_M=\kappa_M^{-1}\circ D_{\theta,M}^{-1}$. Adjacent inverse factors cancel to give both inverse identities. Composing the cited naturality equations gives $f^n\Phi_M=\Phi_{M\prime}E(f)$ for every $R$-linear $f:M\to M\prime$.

source.place: Last sentence, first inference: the natural finite-power description of tensor with a finite free coefficient ring

proof.text: For each $i$, the normalized forward coordinate identity for $D_\theta$ and $U\kappa_M\,p_M=t_{N,M}$ give $U(\rho_i\Phi_M)p_M=\gamma_M(Uq_i\otimes\operatorname{id})$. This is precisely the local rule $s\otimes m\mapsto q_i(s)m$. For the inverse, substitute the normalized finite-sum formula for $U(D_{\theta,M}^{-1})$ into $U\Psi_M$; replace $U\kappa_M^{-1}t_{N,M}$ by $p_M$. The resulting sum is $\sum_i p_M((Ue_i\eta_R)\otimes\operatorname{id})\lambda_{UM}^{-1}U\rho_i$, which sends $(m_i)$ to $\sum_i b_i\otimes m_i$ since $b_i=e_i(1)$. These are identities through the coequalizer projections, hence specify sheaf morphisms as asserted.

proof.text: The relative-tensor coordinate lemma includes $n=0$. Thus this same composite and its normalized formulas apply to the empty finite product and empty sum, without a positivity assumption. No sectionwise tensor identification is used.
